setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named at the open — 'already got some information from Kim, but I just want to have a general conversation with you' — and her notes were used twice during the call: 'of course, Kim already mentioned it as well. Like it's more like the chronic side, right?' and 'from what Kim told me, it sounds like it's a hard time in the morning to get started, to get moving.' The prospect also confirms prior contact: 'you've already been chatting, of course, with Kim.'

prospect.name: Andy Wall
prospect.location: Mountains of Costa Rica; American expatriate, moved in 2023
prospect.family_status: Married; his wife Missy, a nurse, joined the call and participated throughout. They have children and grandchildren.
prospect.training_background: Has worked out his whole life and intends to continue regardless of the outcome of this call — 'whether I do this program or not, I'm still going to always do something.' Currently trains with bodyweight and resistance bands: sets of 100 reps with 30-second rests on tricep pressdowns, shoulder presses and curls, plus 100-200 squats including Bulgarian split squats and air squats, all unweighted. Yoga once a week with his wife. Does Trevor's five-minute mobility routine most mornings. Recently bought kettlebells and has followed a few of Trevor's YouTube videos, including weighted squats with a 35 lb bell. Completed the pre-call assessment well — a 1 minute 45 second dead hang and a two-minute deep squat hold against a one-minute target.
prospect.medical: Extensive surgical history: back surgery in 2020 for a herniated disc, four separate shoulder surgeries, a hernia repair and a knee operation. The back pain returned shortly after the 2020 surgery and has persisted. A 2023 MRI showed the herniation had resolved; he has since self-diagnosed using ChatGPT, which suggested degenerative disc disease and arthritis, and no clinician has confirmed this. He has not seen a specialist — 'I haven't really been to a specialist, other than I've had some assessments.' Current pain is 4 to 5 out of 10 on waking, dropping to about 2 with movement; he cannot lift his own leg into trousers or put socks on in the morning without using his hands. Describes himself as in a constant state of inflammation, severely inflexible through hamstrings and hip flexors, and states 'I fear loading my spine anymore.' His back 'kills' him when holding his grandchildren. Takes ibuprofen or anti-inflammatories once or twice a week and deliberately limits it. His wife additionally disclosed high LDL cholesterol as a caution during the nutrition discussion.

signals: Older, health-literate and living in a medically informed household — his wife is a nurse, took notes throughout, raised his cholesterol unprompted and corrected the record on his MRI history
Goal is relief and retained function rather than gain: 'if something he does gets rid of back pain, that's the number one. And then, you know, the fitness and anything else would just be a bonus'
Already managing actively rather than neglecting — daily mobility routine, weekly yoga, lifelong training habit, deliberate limits on anti-inflammatories, no fast food
Framing is about not losing further ground: asked where continuing as he is leaves him in ten years, he answered 'It won't get me any farther. You know, I'll just be, you know, status quo'
Retired with means but real price sensitivity — expected $2,000-3,000 and reacted to $6,000 with 'Wow. I thought it would be less than that'
Departs from the archetype in one respect that matters: he described himself as 'kind of desperate', which is closer to rescue than to preservation and is why he scores outside the stated ICP

goals.text: Eliminate chronic back pain — stated as goal number one, with everything else a bonus
Wake up and be able to dress without lifting his leg into his trousers by hand
Regain flexibility, particularly hamstrings and hip flexors
Be able to pick up and play with his grandchildren without his back hurting
Keep hiking and stay active with his wife and family
Learn correct kettlebell form so he does not make the back worse
Stop relying on ibuprofen and anti-inflammatories
Learn enough to continue independently — 'just teach me what I need to know and then I'll move on by myself'
Stay mobile and functional into older age rather than accepting decline as inevitable

pains.text: Chronic back pain persisting for years, 4-5 out of 10 on waking, following 2020 back surgery for a herniated disc that initially worked then relapsed
Five prior surgeries — back, four shoulders, plus a hernia and a knee
Cannot put on trousers, socks or shoes in the morning without lifting his leg with his hands
Explicitly afraid to load his spine — 'I fear loading my spine anymore'
Severe inflexibility through hamstrings and hip flexors that reverts within days of any gains
Describes himself as being in a constant state of inflammation
Back hurts when holding his grandchildren, and he pushes through it rather than stopping
Self-diagnosed degenerative disc disease and arthritis via ChatGPT, with no clinician consulted since 2023
High LDL cholesterol, raised as a caution by his wife
Describes himself as desperate — 'I'll try anything. I'm kind of desperate'
Tends to overeat and cannot sustain a true intermittent fast because of coffee with cream and sugar and a daily scoop of peanut butter
Every previous flexibility approach — yoga, YouTube programmes, wall work — produced gains that reverted

objections.raw_quote: 6k overall? Wow. I thought it would be less than that. So $6,000. Wow. Okay. I was thinking around two, two or between two and three, but okay, so it's twice as much as I thought.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged the gap and moved to structure rather than defending the value — 'Most guys do that overall. It's like a hard must... Like we don't have anything set in stone, but if it only comes down to the cost and you feel like, yes, I do want to do this, it's just like too much to just go for up front, then we could split it up.'

objections.raw_quote: Well, my thinking is if it doesn't work, if it does, if it's not for me, I don't have any recourse, you know, I can't, I can't say no.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed the underlying need — 'is it like, you just want to make sure that it is actually working within like the first month? And if not, you can just pull out from it' — then improvised a 30-day exit inside an instalment structure: pay $1,200 for month one, then either settle $4,800 or stop. Also cited the continue-until-results guarantee.

objections.raw_quote: I could put it like this, I could continue to watch YouTube videos for a lot cheaper. Because I do follow him on a day, Trevor, on a daily basis. And he always puts his workouts in the captions, you know.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the free content works — 'if you follow the YouTube, you can see results, 100%. Otherwise, you wouldn't post it' — then reframed against the cost of a second back surgery: 'if you want to make sure you actually get the results that you want and you don't have to get surgery again, then I think in the long run, this is going to cost less.' The prospect had already conceded the point himself before the rebuttal.

objections.raw_quote: he wouldn't begin at least till August 1st. Yeah, I can [not] begin till August 1st because we're going back to the United States for a couple weeks and going to be going from place to place. And these places won't have kettlebells.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the constraint without challenge and worked with it, booking a follow-up for 30 July to allow an 1 August start. Given a genuine two-plus-week trip with no equipment access, this is defensible judgement rather than a missed play.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Six instalments with a $200 monthly premium: 'we split it up into six, basically. It does go up a little bit with 200 a month in that sense. But then for the first month, it would be 1,200.' Carried to term that totals $7,200 against a $6,000 offer. Early settlement was offered — pay $1,200 for month one then $4,800 to clear, returning the total to $6,000. Bundled with an improvised 30-day exit: 'if you feel like, yeah, I want to keep doing this... we just do it afterwards, or we find out any different way, and if not, then we would just stop it right there.' The rep explicitly declined a one-week trial as too short to show results.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated as: 'Usually six months, but if we don't get to the set goals, even though you've put in all the effort that you should be putting in, then Trevor would stay coaching you until you actually get to those goals. But overall, it's six months.'

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent.
A follow-up call was booked live for 30 July at 2pm the prospect's time, and the calendar invite was sent and confirmed received during the call.
Start date deferred by the prospect to 1 August because of a two-week US trip with no equipment access.
Interest confirmed as high but the decision explicitly joint and pending: 'it's not out of reach. It's something we could figure out, but it's just something we'd have to talk about.'
Prospect asked for exactly this outcome: 'Do you give a time to think about it, and then I get back a hold of you later?'

Counter-evidence pointing to a live deal: he described himself as 'kind of desperate', rated his interest 'pretty high', accepted the 30-day exit as addressing his recourse concern, and said 'we'll probably make a decision here in a little while'. The rep also confirmed in a setter debrief thirteen minutes later that he expects it may still close this month.

Counter-evidence against: he experienced genuine price shock at twice his expectation, and he stated he will continue training regardless — 'whether I do this program or not, I'm still going to always do something.'
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call booked for 30 July at 2pm local; prospect and his wife to discuss the cost in the meantime; intended programme start 1 August. Rep gave his phone number and email and offered to send content in the interim.

notable.note: The heaviest clinical picture in the batch, sold to on the strength of pain relief. Five prior surgeries including a 2020 spinal operation, chronic daily back pain, self-diagnosis of degenerative disc disease and arthritis obtained from ChatGPT, no specialist seen, high LDL cholesterol raised by his nurse wife, and an explicit statement that he fears loading his spine. To his credit the rep said 'we're not clinical people' and asked whether a specialist had been consulted — the only such question in the batch — but on hearing 'I haven't really been to a specialist' he rephrased his own question away from the subject and never returned to it, never suggested seeking clearance, and immediately added 'we know it works'. He then positioned the programme as avoiding a second back surgery. Commercially, the same $200-per-month instalment premium and the same improvised first-month exit appear here as on the 07/02 call, a day apart. A claim that two people doing the programme together would halve the price was also made near the end and left uncorrected.

quality.notes: Two speakers share the single label 'Andy Wall' — the prospect and his wife Missy are never distinguished, so her contributions (raising the cholesterol, correcting his MRI history, 'I don't think it's ever stopped you', 'he does have high cholesterol') sit under his name and were separated by content. On top of that the usual rep-prospect inversion runs throughout, most severely from 00:01:03 to 00:02:11 where the entire back-history exchange alternates within single blocks, and again from 00:38:40 to 00:39:20. All roles resolved from content. Speaker attribution at 00:55:08 is genuinely ambiguous and matters: the line 'Maybe I can talk her into doing the program, and then that'll cut the price in half if two people are doing it' is labelled as the rep but reads more naturally as the prospect; on either reading it was not corrected. No age, height or weight was ever established. Heavy rain on a metal roof degraded audio mid-call and the participants moved rooms and switched to shared earbuds.
